newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices slow, volatility up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices slow, volatility up.

text.p: U.S. stock index trading was relatively quiet despite the market's gyrations, traders said Thursday.
But the choppiness drove volatility higher, as evidenced by the Chicago Board Options Exchange's volatility index, which climbed 1.10 to 18.35, its highest closing level since early September.
One trader said some investors moved to the sidelines as the Dow industrial average fell, then erased its gain only to slump again in the afternoon and close down.
The blue chip barometer lost 44 points, or about 0.75 percent, to end at 5,992.
"Index options were quiet. Nothing was jumping out at us," one trader in Chicago said.
Marty Kearney at PTI Securities said most of the action in S&P 100 index options was not surprising given the market's action.
The OEX fell more than six points to close at about 678.
The most active OEX option was the November 680 put, which traded 19,240 contracts. The November 675 put traded 10,409.
"It's normal to have a lot of interest in the slightly out-of-the-money puts," Kearney said.
The busiest OEX options on the call side were the November 685 and November 690, which traded 11,636 and 10,351 contracts, respectively.
OEX options volume tailed off dramatically after the November series, with the most active contract outside November being the January 680 put, which traded 629 contracts.
On the S&P 500 stock index traded at the CBOE, puts continued to dominate, with 41,201 contracts changing hands compared with 20,094 calls.
The SPX ended down about five points at 702, just off its low for the day.
Activity in SPX options was scattered, but a heavy concentration was seen in the most active November 725 calls, which traded 10,870 contracts on the CBOE.
